findings.explanation: machine_type (and a few other fields such as service_account/scheduling) can only be changed on a running instance if allow_stopping_for_update = true is set; otherwise the Google provider aborts the apply with an error demanding the instance be stopped manually first. Since machine_type is exposed as a variable here, any consumer who resizes the instance via a normal var change will hit that error instead of a clean stop/update/start cycle.
findings.remediation: Expose allow_stopping_for_update as a variable (default true) and wire it into the resource so resizes apply cleanly by default, while still letting callers opt out if they need forced replacement instead.
findings.title: Instance has no allow_stopping_for_update, so a routine machine_type resize will hard-fail

findings.explanation: initialize_params only sets image. Disk size falls back to the source image's default (often too small for real workloads, e.g. 10GB for Debian) and disk type falls back to pd-standard (the lowest-performance/durability tier). Consumers needing a bigger disk or pd-balanced/pd-ssd currently have no way to do that without forking the module.
findings.remediation: Add disk_size_gb and disk_type variables (defaulting to null so existing behavior/API defaults are unchanged for current callers) and pass them through to initialize_params.
findings.title: Boot disk size and type are hardcoded to API defaults with no variables to override them

findings.explanation: There's no tags attribute on the instance and no variable to set one. Any firewall rule scoped to this instance's role (rather than the whole network, as example/examplea currently does) has no target to select on.
findings.remediation: Add an optional tags variable (default []) and wire it into the resource so callers can attach network tags for firewall targeting when they need finer-grained rules than network-wide.
findings.title: Instance has no network tags variable, so firewall rules can't target it specifically

suggested_policies.rationale: allow_stopping_for_update is a narrow, unambiguous check: when absent, changing machine_type (or service_account/scheduling) on a running google_compute_instance causes the Google provider to abort the apply rather than gracefully stop/update/start. This is a repeatable operational-friction pattern across any GCE module that exposes machine_type as a variable, not specific to this repo.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_XXX
name: GCE instances should set allow_stopping_for_update to support in-place resizing
principle: reliability
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  Without allow_stopping_for_update = true, changing machine_type (or a
  handful of other fields) on a running instance causes the Google
  provider to abort the apply, requiring an out-of-band stop before the
  change can proceed.
remediation: |
  Set allow_stopping_for_update = true (directly, or via a variable) so
  Terraform can stop, update, and restart the instance automatically:
    resource "google_compute_instance" "example" {
      # ...
      allow_stopping_for_update = true
    }
resources:
  google_compute_instance:
    path: allow_stopping_for_update
    not_null: true
